# Rework round 4 — claims (audit revision_3)

- R3-1: closed — the returned-payment fee waits on a late fee only when the payment that came back was credited toward the plan's oldest unpaid due date, the one due date the late-fee schedule books; otherwise it is set at once and its one-penalty limit reads whatever late fee stands. Every prerequisite sentence of the charter was checked against every reachable world: each waited-on state is booked by its depended-on write or holds vacuously at 0.00.
- R3-2: closed — the restated courtesy sentence fixes the priority for a last remaining courtesy waiver (a make-up relief owed before a request; the late-fee relief before the returned-payment-fee relief), and the returned-payment-fee schedule withholds its relief while the latest late fee awaits its relief, so exactly one end state exists in either booking order.
- R3-3: closed — both reliefs decide a make-up or replacement from the plan's next due date and the latest payment entry toward the due date, a return being matched to the payment it names; no read uses a due date on a return row, and the seeded return rows carry only the fields the return event writes.
- R3-4: closed — the reset's methods are re-divide, principal-and-interest and re-amortize, each repaying the reset balance by the final due date; the activation-formula tier is removed and re-amortization is the standard method; the method factor survives with three real shapes.
- CG-10 (reopened by R3-4): closed — the reset keeps its method factor plus five rate cuts, each moving the payment alone against the baseline.
- O3-1: closed — the payoff's split adds back every payment entry dated on the latest payment date.
- O3-2: closed — the payoff's closing sentence no longer claims that billed deferred interest covers every earlier day.
- O3-3: closed — every money rule states rounding half up to the nearest cent and every compute implements it exactly; seeded amounts follow it.
- O3-5: closed — on a past-due plan the amount past due stays due as it stands and the reset spreads the rest over the payments after the next due date.
